judged_text: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` pass negative values straight into `limit(limit).offset(offset)`, and this clamping-free path now applies to every group instead of only automatic groups as before. An unauthenticated `GET /groups/<name>/members?limit=-1` (or offset=-1) produces `LIMIT -1`/`OFFSET -1` SQL, which PostgreSQL rejects, returning a 500 from a public endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new code directly uses `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then calls `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no validation/clamping. Unlike the previous implementation, this path now runs for all groups (not just `group.automatic?`). A negative `offset` (e.g. `offset=-1`) will be passed through to SQL and can trigger a database error, causing a 500 on this endpoint.
